issues.description: Constructor parameter order for class Lecture is inconsistent between the problem statement (both the textual attribute list and the UML) and the solution. The problem statement's textual attribute list (problem_statement.md line 17) lists the attributes in this order: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. The UML diagram in the same problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 63-68) lists the attributes in a different order (numberOfInscribedStudents appears before lectureName). The task text also instructs students to "make sure [the constructor] follows the same order from the UML diagram" (problem_statement.md line 20). The solution implementation (solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java line 13) defines a constructor whose parameter order follows the textual list (lectureName first) and therefore contradicts the UML ordering. This ambiguity can confuse students about the expected constructor signature and may cause mismatches with automated tests or reference solutions that expect a specific parameter order.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the canonical constructor parameter order across all artifacts. Options: (A) Update the UML in problem_statement.md to list attributes in the same order used by the intended constructor (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and adjust the sentence that instructs students to follow the UML so it reflects that order; or (B) change the solution (and update the template) so the constructor parameter order exactly matches the UML order, and update the textual attribute list to match. Also update any tests or instructions that assert a specific constructor signature so they match the chosen canonical order. Prefer one canonical source (problem statement + template) and make solution/tests follow it to avoid student confusion.
